lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが半濁点、つまり「゜」の書き方を教えて下さった
lines.en: Gran, when your father was young, he taught me how to write handakuten—the marks like this: ゜
lines.style: Soft, nostalgic opening. Measured, reflective pace. Quiet reverence for a small memory. Linger slightly on the detail, as if seeing it again.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん、お祖父ちゃん、若い頃、片仮名のヽ、つまり繰り返し記号を使われたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Yes, and your grandfather, when he was young, he used to use the iteration mark in katakana—ヽ—didn't he, dear?
lines.style: Warm, knowing smile in the voice. Gentle test—checking if he remembers too. Light, companionable. A small laugh hovering at the edge.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが平仮名のゞ、つまり濁点繰り返しを書かれた
lines.en: Gran, when your father was young, he used to write the voiced iteration mark in hiragana—ゞ.
lines.style: Steady, almost gentle correction. Not contradicting her, just adding his own thread. Same quiet reverence. A little slower on the technical detail.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、若い頃、平仮名のゝ、つまり繰り返し記号を使われたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Your grandfather, when he was young, he used the iteration mark in hiragana—ゝ—didn't he, dear?
lines.style: Warm persistence. She's building her own catalogue now. Light, playful insistence. Voice stays bright, patient.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが片仮名のヾ、つまり濁点繰り返しに詳しかった
lines.en: Gran, when your father was young, he knew quite a lot about the voiced iteration mark in katakana—ヾ.
lines.style: Quiet admiration underneath. Slight lift on 「詳しかった」—pride in his father's knowledge. Warm but measured. The respect of one learned person remembering another.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、若い頃、旧仮名のゐを使ってお手紙を書かれたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Your grandfather, when he was young, he used to write letters using the old kana ゐ, didn't he, dear?
lines.style: Delighted by the memory. Lifting slightly on 「書かれたわよね」. She's enjoying this back-and-forth. Voice stays warm, a little teasing in the affection.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんはゐる、つまり古文の「いる」を仰った
lines.en: Gran, when your father was young, he used to say ゐる—the old word for 'to be' in classical Japanese.
lines.style: Careful, precise. He's preserving this. Quiet weight on the pronunciation. A little slower, reverential. The voice of someone keeping something alive.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、若い頃、爾、つまり古文の「それ」を読まれたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Your grandfather, when he was young, he used to read 爾—the old classical word for 'that'—didn't he, dear?
lines.style: Final warm note. Soft laugh underneath. She's had the last word, and they both know it. Close with a tender, satisfied smile in her voice.
